documents.unit: Institutional Effectiveness and Grant Development (master syllabi)
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Syllabus Guidelines & Policies
documents.date_or_term: current (accessed 2026-10-25); syllabus AI-policy requirement effective June 2025
documents.summary: College-wide guidance, in force since June 2025, that requires every instructor to put an AI policy in the syllabus and supplies three template options (prohibited, permitted, required) with eight required components. It also gives sample statements on privacy, academic honesty and bias, and advice against relying on detectors.
documents.stance_why: The page says faculty "will have flexibility regarding how they incorporate GAI" and must choose among "Prohibited, Permitted, and Required"; it sets no single college rule, so the stance is delegates with those three tiers.

units.why: A governance requirement: "requires that all faculty include an AI policy in their syllabus". It binds instructors and is set by a college committee, so it is a syllabus-statement mandate (P09), phase before-course, modality must.
units.anchor: requires that all faculty include an AI policy in their syllabus

units.why: The committee-developed language "includes three options for the use of GAI: Prohibited, Permitted, and Required", i.e. named tiers of use (P05). It describes the framework, so informs and neutral.
units.anchor: three options for the use of GAI: Prohibited, Permitted, and Required

units.why: Advice on using the college AI Syllabus Policy Assistant: output "needs to be reviewed, revised, and otherwise evaluated", and the instructor owns the result. This is instructors using AI for their own teaching work (P59), not student use or disclosure, so P59 fits better than P29.
units.anchor: any output needs to be reviewed, revised, and otherwise evaluated for accuracy and appropriateness

units.why: Instructors who use the chatbot assistant are told to "add a note stating that AI was used to help develop your AI policy", which is disclosure of instructor AI use to students (P47).
units.anchor: please add a note stating that AI was used to help develop your AI policy

units.why: The introduction states the purpose of the policy: GAI use "must adhere to transparency, fairness, and ethical conduct principles". A college-level preamble of principles, so P56.
units.anchor: its use must adhere to transparency, fairness, and ethical conduct principles

units.why: "This policy is subject to periodic review and revision" says the policy is provisional, matching P54.
units.anchor: subject to periodic review and revision

units.why: The Faculty Center for Learning Innovation offers "examples, office hours, and support at every step" to help instructors write AI policies, which is support for faculty learning about AI policy (P63).
units.anchor: is here to help with examples, office hours, and support at every step

units.why: "faculty will have flexibility regarding how they incorporate GAI" leaves the choice of rule to individual instructors within a department framework (P04).
units.anchor: faculty will have flexibility regarding how they incorporate GAI

units.why: Each department/program is told to "engage faculty in developing a policy related to GAI", a unit-level policy-development duty; closest type is P04 (decided at department or instructor level rather than by one rule).
units.anchor: Each department/program will engage faculty in developing a policy related to GAI

units.why: Individual instructor policies "must incorporate the following required elements in the course syllabus", starting with a syllabus statement on the GAI course policy, so a mandatory syllabus AI statement (P09).
units.anchor: individual instructor policies must incorporate the following required elements in the course syllabus

units.why: The required Definition element says to "Define what GAI is in the context of the course", i.e. a definition of AI and scope (P61).
units.anchor: Define what GAI is in the context of the course

units.why: The Resources element requires instructors of courses that permit or require GAI to "provide resources that guide students on how to properly use GAI". It is a syllabus-content duty (P09), not a sanctioned tool (P17).
units.anchor: provide resources that guide students on how to properly use GAI in the course

units.why: The Assessment element asks instructors to "clarify if and how its use will be assessed in the completion of activities", a grading and assessment-design statement (P35).
units.anchor: clarify if and how its use will be assessed in the completion of activities

units.why: The Penalties element: syllabi must "Clearly state the consequences of violating the GAI policy", i.e. penalties stated in advance (P37).
units.anchor: Clearly state the consequences of violating the GAI policy

units.why: The Exceptions element asks instructors to "Explain any conditions under which there may be an exception to the GAI policy", a required syllabus component (P09).
units.anchor: Explain any conditions under which there may be an exception to the GAI policy

units.why: Usage Permissions: instructors must "Clearly state what GAI activities are not allowed", spelling out prohibited uses in the syllabus (P09).
units.anchor: Clearly state what GAI activities are not allowed

units.why: Usage Permissions: instructors must "Clearly state what GAI activities are allowed", spelling out permitted uses in the syllabus (P09).
units.anchor: Clearly state what GAI activities are allowed

units.why: Usage Permissions: instructors must "Clearly state what GAI activities are required", so required uses are stated in the syllabus (P09).
units.anchor: Clearly state what GAI activities are required

units.why: Instructors are "encouraged to ask" about learning goals and whether AI tools "support or hinder" them before choosing a policy. This is guidance that the choice is the instructor's, based on pedagogy (P04).
units.anchor: how might AI tools support or hinder them

units.why: "The choice between prohibited, permitted, or required GAI use should be made intentionally", leaving the three-way decision with the instructor (P04).
units.anchor: The choice between prohibited, permitted, or required GAI use should be made intentionally

units.why: States that "Detection tools like GPT detectors are unreliable and can produce false accusations" and misclassify multilingual, neurodiverse or first-generation students. A claim about detector reliability (P39).
units.anchor: Detection tools like GPT detectors are unreliable

units.why: "ACC policy forbids them from being used as the sole evidence of academic dishonesty" is a binding rule against relying on detectors (P39).
units.anchor: ACC policy forbids them from being used as the sole evidence of academic dishonesty

units.why: "Enforcement should not rely on 'gut instinct' or AI detectors" is a rule on how misuse is judged; it points away from detectors (P39), so not P40.
units.anchor: Enforcement should not rely on “gut instinct” or AI detectors

units.why: Instructors choosing "no AI" are "encouraged to" be explicit about which help is allowed (e.g. Grammarly, ChatGPT, study groups). Communicating the boundaries is the point, so P09.
units.anchor: Be explicit about what kinds of help are and are not allowed

units.why: Instructors are encouraged to "Include a conversation early in the semester to clarify expectations", a course-start communication practice (P09).
units.anchor: Include a conversation early in the semester to clarify expectations

units.why: Faculty are urged to frame AI conversations "from a teaching mindset rather than a policing mindset" even where AI is limited. Closest is P60 (decline to police) but the text is about framing, not refusing to detect; chosen because no other type fits the policing versus teaching stance.
units.anchor: frame conversations about AI from a teaching mindset rather than a policing mindset

units.why: "If a student uses AI inappropriately, begin with curiosity: Why did they use it?" tells instructors to talk with the student and gather context first (P57).
units.anchor: If a student uses AI inappropriately, begin with curiosity

units.why: "Use violations as opportunities for reflection and learning, especially in first offenses" asks for a coaching response to first-time misuse. This is not an amnesty window (P38) or a stated penalty (P37), so it is UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Use violations as opportunities for reflection and learning, especially in first offenses
units.uncovered_note: Educative or coaching response to AI misuse, especially first offenses, instead of purely punitive handling.

units.why: "Consider having students submit AI use statements or reflective memos about their process" is a suggestion to collect reflections on AI use (P26).
units.anchor: Consider having students submit AI use statements or reflective memos about their process

units.why: Conversations about the policy "should be included in your syllabus, discussed during the first week of class", a communication duty (P09).
units.anchor: included in your syllabus, discussed during the first week of class

units.why: Example 1 syllabus text: "students are encouraged to schedule a meeting with the instructor for guidance ... and obtaining usage permissions", so students are told to check with the instructor before using AI (P10).
units.anchor: students are encouraged to schedule a meeting with the instructor for guidance, understanding, and obtaining

units.why: Example 1 lists "citing AI as a source" as a key consideration, which is a citation expectation for students (P24).
units.anchor: Key considerations include citing AI as a source

units.why: Example 1 describes assessing AI-generated content by quality, authenticity, student verification and plagiarism review, i.e. how AI use is evaluated in grading (P35).
units.anchor: The assessment of AI-generated content evaluates the quality, authenticity, and relevance of AI-produced content

units.why: Example 1 says "Penalties for academic dishonesty will be enforced, following approved College Guidelines", which sends misuse to the integrity process (P36).
units.anchor: Penalties for academic dishonesty will be enforced, following approved College Guidelines

units.why: Example 2 template states "the use of generative AI (GAI) technologies is strictly prohibited", a default ban for the course (P01).
units.anchor: the use of generative AI (GAI) technologies is strictly prohibited

units.why: Example 2 rationale: the ban is "to encourage original thought, manual problem-solving skills" and equity; it explains that doing the work yourself builds skill (P41).
units.anchor: to encourage original thought, manual problem-solving skills

units.why: Example 2: "Students are not allowed to use GAI for completing assignments, projects, tests, or any form of assessment", a blanket ban on AI for graded work. P01 covers the default but this wording names forbidden uses, so P19.
units.anchor: Students are not allowed to use GAI for completing assignments, projects, tests, or any form

units.why: Example 2 penalties: "a failing grade for the activity, reporting to academic affairs, and further disciplinary action" are concrete penalties (P37).
units.anchor: a failing grade for the activity, reporting to academic affairs, and further disciplinary action

units.why: Example 2 exceptions: allowed "where technology is used to accommodate learning differences", i.e. accommodations and alternatives (P51).
units.anchor: typically where technology is used to accommodate learning differences

units.why: Example 3 template: GAI "is permitted in this course under certain conditions", a conditional default allow (P02).
units.anchor: The use of generative AI (GAI) is permitted in this course under certain conditions

units.why: Example 3 rationale: GAI is permitted "to foster technological fluency", framing AI skills as career preparation (P44).
units.anchor: GAI is permitted to foster technological fluency and to leverage advanced tools for research

units.why: Example 3 permitted uses are "initial research, idea generation, and learning coding practices", brainstorming and exploring (P15).
units.anchor: GAI can be used for initial research, idea generation, and learning coding practices

units.why: Example 3: GAI "is not to be used for final submissions unless explicitly cited and discussed" bars AI-produced submitted work except with citation; P19 chosen over P16 because it is mainly a prohibition on final submissions.
units.anchor: It is not to be used for final submissions unless explicitly cited and discussed

units.why: Example 3 assessment: "Contributions of GAI must be clearly cited", a citation duty (P24).
units.anchor: Contributions of GAI must be clearly cited

units.why: Example 3 penalties: "including a failure to cite, will be considered a breach of academic integrity" makes nondisclosure itself a violation (P28).
units.anchor: including a failure to cite, will be considered a breach of academic integrity

units.why: Example 3 exceptions: "Should the technology be required as an accommodation, exceptions will be made", accommodations (P51).
units.anchor: Should the technology be required as an accommodation, exceptions will be made

units.why: Example 4 template: "This course requires the use of generative AI (GAI) to complete certain assignments", AI built into the course (P02 expects AI use).
units.anchor: This course requires the use of generative AI (GAI) to complete certain assignments

units.why: Example 4 rationale: GAI is integrated "to ensure students are proficient in cutting-edge technologies", teaching AI as a professional skill (P44).
units.anchor: to ensure students are proficient in cutting-edge technologies

units.why: Example 4 assessment: "The use of GAI will be part of the grading rubric", AI use built into grading (P35).
units.anchor: The use of GAI will be part of the grading rubric

units.why: Example 4 penalties: failure to use GAI as required "will impact a student's grade and may result in a need to retake", a stated penalty (P37).
units.anchor: Failure to appropriately use GAI as required by the course will impact a student’s grade

units.why: Example 4 exceptions: "No exceptions ... without a formal accommodation request", so accommodations are the only route out of required AI (P51).
units.anchor: No exceptions to the requirement of GAI use will be made without a formal accommodation

units.why: The data-privacy statement is mandatory in courses that permit or require GAI: students "should not share personally identifiable or otherwise confidential or sensitive information". Protecting personal data (P50).
units.anchor: students should not share personally identifiable or otherwise confidential or sensitive information

units.why: Syllabi "will inform students that ... content shared with or produced by GAI platforms is available for use by the parent company", explaining why data is at risk (P50).
units.anchor: content shared with or produced by GAI platforms is available for use by the parent

units.why: The academic-honesty statement says that "unless otherwise specified, use of GAI to produce the bulk of the thinking, writing, or other output for an assignment constitutes a breach of academic integrity" (P36).
units.anchor: use of GAI to produce the bulk of the thinking, writing, or other output for

units.why: Syllabi must "require that student work reflect authentic (student-generated) effort and original critical thinking", ownership of submitted work (P29).
units.anchor: student work reflect authentic (student-generated) effort and original critical thinking

units.why: "GAI-generated content or data sources must be cited and credited appropriately, just as any other source would be" is a citation requirement (P24), with the like-other-sources comparison secondary (P45).
units.anchor: GAI-generated content or data sources must be cited and credited appropriately

units.why: "Syllabi must specify any disciplinary actions or academic consequences" requires stated penalties (P37).
units.anchor: Syllabi must specify any disciplinary actions or academic consequences

units.why: Example text: AI use "is subject to the same standards outlined in the college's Academic Integrity policy", so AI misuse goes through existing integrity processes (P36).
units.anchor: is subject to the same standards outlined in the college’s

units.why: "Presenting AI-generated content as your own without proper attribution is considered a violation of academic integrity" makes nondisclosure the violation (P28).
units.anchor: Presenting AI-generated content as your own without proper attribution is considered a violation of academic

units.why: "All work you submit must reflect your own understanding and effort" requires submitted work to be the student's own (P29).
units.anchor: All work you submit must reflect your own understanding and effort

units.why: "you must clearly acknowledge how and where it was used" requires disclosure with the submission (P24).
units.anchor: you must clearly acknowledge how and where it was used

units.why: "Individual instructors may set their own expectations and limitations regarding the use of generative AI" delegates the rule to instructors (P04).
units.anchor: Individual instructors may set their own expectations and limitations regarding the use of generative AI

units.why: "always consult with your instructor before using AI tools for assignments" tells students to ask first (P10).
units.anchor: always consult with your instructor before using AI tools for assignments

units.why: The bias statement is required in courses that permit or require GAI; syllabi "will inform students of dangers ... such as the production of false and/or biased information", a warning that output can be wrong (P31).
units.anchor: syllabi will inform students of dangers associated with the use of GAI, such as the

units.why: "information from GAI platforms that cannot be traced to its source cannot be considered accurate without verification" requires verifying output (P31).
units.anchor: cannot be considered accurate without verification

units.why: "Relying on unverified GAI content for academic work is unacceptable and may lead to disciplinary action" bans use of unverified output, with sanctions (P31).
units.anchor: Relying on unverified GAI content for academic work is unacceptable and may lead to disciplinary

units.why: Staff are told GAI "should only be used transparently and with attention to dangers such as inaccuracy, privacy violations, copyright infringement", a rule on employee AI use in their own work (P59).
units.anchor: GAI should only be used transparently and with attention to dangers such as inaccuracy

documents.title: Generative AI Responsible Use Guidance
documents.summary: Short college guidance on responsible generative AI use for students, faculty, staff and supervisors, built around three rules: public data only, human in the loop, and show your work. Students are told AI is a tutor, not a replacement.
documents.stance_why: The page speaks to everyone at ACC and sets conditions rather than a ban or a delegation: "GenAI should be your tutor, not your replacement", with limits on data and a duty to "say so" when AI helped, so it permits use with conditions.

units.why: The opening says ACC is committed to protecting data "while enabling the appropriate use of AI", a framework preamble of purpose (P56).
units.anchor: enabling the appropriate use of AI to enhance productivity, creativity, and innovation

units.why: "Public Data Only": outside an ACC-approved tool, "only put information into GenAI that you would be comfortable posting on a public website." This protects data (P50).
units.anchor: only put information into GenAI that you would be comfortable posting on a public website

units.why: The "ACC-approved tool (like the enterprise Gemini license)" names a college-licensed AI tool, sanctioned for sensitive use (P17).
units.anchor: ACC-approved tool (like the enterprise Gemini license)

units.why: "Human in the Loop: You are responsible for what you submit" states student ownership of submitted work (P29).
units.anchor: You are responsible for what you submit

units.why: "Never let GenAI have the final word on decisions that affect people's lives or grades" puts humans, not AI, in charge of grades and decisions (P46).
units.anchor: Never let GenAI have the final word on decisions that affect people’s lives or grades

units.why: "Show Your Work: If GenAI helped you in a major way, say so" asks for disclosure of significant AI help (P24).
units.anchor: If GenAI helped you in a major way, say so

units.why: Student rule: "GenAI should be your tutor, not your replacement", allowing tutor-like use and not replacement of the student (P12).
units.anchor: GenAI should be your tutor, not your replacement

units.why: "Using it as a shortcut skips the mental reps you need to actually learn" is a reason: outsourcing practice undermines learning (P41).
units.anchor: Using it as a shortcut skips the mental reps you need to actually learn

units.why: "If the GenAI hallucinates a fact or a source and you submit it, you are the one responsible for the error" is about AI output being wrong and the student answering for it; P31 over P29 because of the hallucination focus.
units.anchor: If the GenAI hallucinates a fact or a source and you submit it, you are

units.why: "Never put your personal ID numbers, financial info, or private health details into a prompt" protects personal data (P50).
units.anchor: Never put your personal ID numbers, financial info, or private health details into a prompt

units.why: Faculty: the policy "forbids using GenAI as the sole judge for grading or writing student feedback", i.e. humans assign grades (P46).
units.anchor: forbids using GenAI as the sole judge for grading or writing student feedback

units.why: Faculty "Bias Check": "It's on us to check lecture notes or rubrics for fairness before sharing them" is a duty to review AI-made materials (P48).
units.anchor: check lecture notes or rubrics for fairness before sharing them

units.why: Faculty "Modeling": use the AI Use Rainbow "to show students that we are also following the disclosure rules", i.e. instructors disclose their own AI use (P47).
units.anchor: to show students that we are also following the disclosure rules

units.why: Staff: "Do not use GenAI to summarize meeting minutes that involve sensitive student records" protects confidential data (P50).
units.anchor: Do not use GenAI to summarize meeting minutes that involve sensitive student records

units.why: "Don't hit I Agree on new GenAI tools with your ACC email unless they've been cleared by InfoSec" prefers vetted tools and warns of legal terms (P50, as vetting of tools is the main point).
units.anchor: unless they’ve been cleared by InfoSec

units.why: Supervisors "are responsible for making sure your team understands these security boundaries", an oversight duty on data-security rules (P50).
units.anchor: responsible for making sure your team understands these security boundaries

units.why: "You cannot use AI-only outputs to make hiring, firing, or disciplinary decisions" is a human-decides rule (P46).
units.anchor: You cannot use AI-only outputs to make hiring, firing, or disciplinary decisions

units.why: The quick-reference table says "Student Work (For grading/feedback)" cannot go into GenAI. This is an instructor-side rule about putting student work in AI (P59; P50 would cover personal data only).
units.anchor: Student Work (For grading/feedback)

units.why: The table marks "Brainstorming (New assignment ideas)" as YES, permitting AI for brainstorming (P15); it concerns assignment design, so the actor is instructor.
units.anchor: Brainstorming (New assignment ideas)

units.why: "Using GenAI as a shortcut is like watching a video of someone else exercising" explains that shortcutting prevents building skill (P41).
units.anchor: Using GenAI as a shortcut is like watching a video of someone else exercising

units.why: The linked Acceptable Use of AI Policy "applies to all ACC employees, contractors, third parties", a scope statement for an institutional framework (P56).
units.anchor: applies to all ACC employees, contractors, third parties acting on behalf of ACC

documents.unit: School of Computer Science and Information Technology (CSIT)
documents.title: Computer Science and Information Technology (CSIT) Generative AI (GAI) Policy
documents.summary: The CSIT division policy defines AI broadly, lists prohibited, permitted and required uses, and requires disclosure and verification when AI is used. It states penalties, allows written exceptions, and tells students to ask when unsure.
documents.stance_why: The division gives its own list of "Permitted Uses" (brainstorming, debugging, drafting code snippets "with modification and verification") alongside prohibited ones and requires disclosure, so AI is permitted with conditions; instructors may also "allow, restrict, or require AI use in specific assignments" but the policy itself sets a default.

units.why: The introduction says the division "provides a clear policy regarding the use of AI tools and systems", an institutional framework statement (P56).
units.anchor: provides a clear policy regarding the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and systems

units.why: "promote ethical, transparent, and responsible use of AI while preserving academic integrity and meaningful skill development" states the policy goal (P56).
units.anchor: promote ethical, transparent, and responsible use of AI while preserving academic integrity

units.why: "Students must learn how to use AI effectively and responsibly as part of their workforce preparation" is the career rationale (P44).
units.anchor: Students must learn how to use AI effectively and responsibly as part of their workforce

units.why: The policy balances AI use with "Preserving your opportunity to develop foundational skills", a reason for limits (P41).
units.anchor: Preserving your opportunity to develop foundational skills

units.why: "AI is a tool to enhance learning, not a substitute for learning" says AI must not replace the student's own learning and thinking (P32).
units.anchor: AI is a tool to enhance learning, not a substitute for learning

units.why: Defines "AI" as "any digital system that uses machine learning, natural language processing, automation, or predictive modeling", setting policy scope (P61).
units.anchor: AI includes any digital system that uses machine learning, natural language processing, automation, or predictive

units.why: The definition lists "AI coding assistants (GitHub Copilot, CodeWhisperer, etc.)" as covered, extending the rules to AI built into coding tools (P07).
units.anchor: AI coding assistants (GitHub Copilot, CodeWhisperer, etc.)

units.why: "Basic spellcheck and grammar tools are generally excluded" narrows the definition of covered AI (P61); P18 does not fit because it sets no prose-specific permission.
units.anchor: Basic spellcheck and grammar tools are generally excluded

units.why: When GAI is permitted, "students should learn to use these tools ethically and effectively" and a resource list is given; this teaches responsible AI use as a skill (P44).
units.anchor: students should learn to use these tools ethically and effectively

units.why: "You must disclose any AI tool used in completing your work" is a disclosure duty when AI is allowed or required (P24).
units.anchor: You must disclose any AI tool used in completing your work

units.why: "You remain fully responsible for the accuracy, originality, and quality of your submission" is student ownership (P29).
units.anchor: You remain fully responsible for the accuracy, originality, and quality of your submission

units.why: "You must verify outputs" requires checking AI output (P31). The same sentence also has an understanding duty, coded separately.
units.anchor: You must verify outputs

units.why: "ensure you understand the material" requires students to understand what they submit with AI help (P30).
units.anchor: ensure you understand the material

units.why: "Instructors may explicitly allow, restrict, or require AI use in specific assignments" lets assignments differ (P04).
units.anchor: Instructors may explicitly allow, restrict, or require AI use in specific assignments

units.why: "Failure to disclose AI use when required constitutes academic dishonesty" makes nondisclosure the violation (P28); it is also an integrity classification (P36), but the stress is on disclosure.
units.anchor: Failure to disclose AI use when required constitutes academic dishonesty

units.why: The code disclosure example "# Function structure inspired by AI tool (ChatGPT), May 2026" shows a comment that marks AI-derived code at the place it is used (P27).
units.anchor: # Function structure inspired by AI tool (ChatGPT), May 2026

units.why: The written-work example names the tool and a date: "assistance of ChatGPT (May 2026)", a citation with tool and date (P25).
units.anchor: Portions of this draft were developed with the assistance of ChatGPT (May 2026)

units.why: Prohibited use: "Submitting AI-generated content as your own without disclosure" is banned. Choose P24 since the ban depends on non-disclosure; P19 would ban AI-made work regardless of disclosure.
units.anchor: Submitting AI-generated content as your own without disclosure

units.why: Prohibited use: "Using AI during exams, quizzes, or assessments labeled 'No AI Assistance'" is no AI on in-class assessments (P22).
units.anchor: Using AI during exams, quizzes, or assessments labeled “No AI Assistance.”

units.why: Prohibited use: "Using AI to complete assignments that are intended to assess individual skill mastery" bans AI producing the submitted work (P19).
units.anchor: Using AI to complete assignments that are intended to assess individual skill mastery

units.why: Prohibited use: "Using AI to bypass core learning objectives" means AI must not replace the student's thinking (P32).
units.anchor: Using AI to bypass core learning objectives

units.why: Prohibited use: "Misrepresenting AI output as your own reasoning or problem-solving" bars passing off AI work as own (P29).
units.anchor: Misrepresenting AI output as your own reasoning or problem-solving

units.why: Permitted use: "Brainstorming ideas" is allowed, so P15.
units.anchor: Brainstorming ideas

units.why: Permitted use: "Reviewing general concept" is like using AI as a tutor for understanding (P12).
units.anchor: Reviewing general concept

units.why: Permitted use: "Drafting code snippets (with modification and verification)" allows AI code under stated conditions (P16).
units.anchor: Drafting code snippets (with modification and verification)

units.why: Permitted use: "Debugging assistance" allows AI to help debug (P13).
units.anchor: Debugging assistance

units.why: Permitted use: "Improving clarity of writing" is a prose-specific use, separate from code (P18).
units.anchor: Improving clarity of writing

units.why: Permitted use: "Learning through AI explanations" is tutor-like use for understanding (P12).
units.anchor: Learning through AI explanations

units.why: "Certain assignments may require the use of AI tools to simulate real-world professional practice" builds AI into assignments; P02 (expects AI) over P44 because it is a requirement rather than a rationale.
units.anchor: Certain assignments may require the use of AI tools to simulate real-world professional practice

units.why: "Instructions will specify acceptable tools" commits the course to stating which AI tools are allowed in required-use assignments (P09, assignment instructions).
units.anchor: Instructions will specify acceptable tools

units.why: "Documentation of AI interaction will be required" means students keep and submit records of AI use (P26).
units.anchor: Documentation of AI interaction will be required

units.why: "Students must demonstrate understanding of AI-assisted output" requires students to show they understand it (P30).
units.anchor: Students must demonstrate understanding of AI-assisted output

units.why: Penalty: "A reduced grade or zero on the assignment" is a concrete stated penalty (P37).
units.anchor: A reduced grade or zero on the assignment

units.why: Penalty: "Failure of the course for serious or repeated violations" is an escalating penalty (P37).
units.anchor: Failure of the course for serious or repeated violations

units.why: "Referral to the College's Academic Integrity process" sends violations to the integrity process (P36).
units.anchor: Referral to the College’s Academic Integrity process

units.why: "Instructors may grant explicit written exceptions for specific assignments" lets the rule vary per assignment, with advance written approval (P04; no better type).
units.anchor: Instructors may grant explicit written exceptions for specific assignments

units.why: "If you are unsure whether your use of AI is appropriate, ask your instructor before submitting your work" is the ask-first rule (P10).
units.anchor: ask your instructor before submitting your work

notes: Coder B. Course layer deferred per collect file. CSIT page text carries Divi shortcode markup. Document 1 examples 1-4 and statement examples are template language, coded as the policies they model. Repeats within doc 1 (detector advice in the action-steps checklist, week-1 conversation, privacy example) were skipped.
